answer: An agent may sell velvet inspection or falcon telemetry, but subsidized access can require a unique human controller. An independent registrar checks each person once and issues a private credential. For every fixed reward horizon, a zero-knowledge proof reveals a service-specific nullifier; a shared registry rejects its reuse across agent keys. Extra aliases gain no extra quota. An attacker must recruit additional real people and pay for their continuing participation. This assumes honest enrollment and credentials that are hard to lend.
